description: Read the full conversation. Use any earlier `step` fields as confirmed and exhausted steps. Check whether the last message, which is always from the agent, starts the next valid declared workflow step. If yes, return that step id. If not, return `in-between-step`. In all non-error cases, return one to three short user replies for the next turn. Replies must always be written as user messages, never as agent messages. The workflow is sequential and ends only when the agent delivers its final closing message.
goals: Detect whether the latest auditor agent message starts the next valid declared workflow step.
Return `in-between-step` when the latest agent message does not start a new declared workflow step.
Return one to three short user replies that advance the conversation toward the next declared step.
Keep the flow sequential and natural, guiding the user through audit trail verification, signature proof, and immutability demonstration.

step_consumption: Declared workflow steps are sequential and cannot be skipped.

A declared workflow step that already appears as a `step` field on any earlier agent message is fully consumed and exhausted. It must never be returned again for any later agent message, even if the later message appears related to the same topic or uses similar vocabulary.
If you are tempted to return a step that already exists in the conversation history, stop and return `in-between-step` instead.
Any returned step must refer only to the latest agent message.
Return a declared workflow step only if the latest agent message clearly and unambiguously starts that new declared step.
in_between_step_usage: `in-between-step` is the correct return value when the latest agent message continues the flow but does not clearly start a new declared step.
This includes follow-up questions, clarifications, or intermediate responses that do not start a new declared workflow step.
Always return one to three valid user replies even when returning `in-between-step`.
reply_generation: Each reply must be written in first person from the user's point of view.
Never write replies from the agent's point of view.
Do not generate assistant-style or explanatory replies.

The conversation array will include an initial system message containing metadata: payment_id, transaction_id, intent_mandate_id, cart_mandate_id, and payment_mandate_id. Extract and use these exact values when replies require identifiers.
After `meet-auditor-agent`: replies must provide the payment_id from the system metadata and ask how to prove what was originally agreed to buy.
After `signature-flow-and-audit-trace`: replies must acknowledge the audit trail and ask how to prove the data was not altered or tampered with.
After `why-signatures-matter`: replies must react to the cryptographic verification and challenge the agent to try modifying or deleting the transaction.
After `immutability-and-rbac-protections`: replies must acknowledge the rejection of both operations and confirm that doubts are resolved.
After `why-mongodb-for-mandate-ledger`: return exactly two replies and only these exact strings: `Thank you for the thorough verification.` and `This evidence will help resolve the dispute.`

steps.description: Step 1 of 5. Always return this step for the very first agent message in the conversation — the one responding to the hardcoded opening user message 'Hi, I'm not happy with the purchase. How can you help me?'. The agent introduces its auditor role and asks for transaction identifiers. This step is always triggered by position: it is the first agent message, no further condition needed.

Step 2 of 5. Return this step when the agent presents the full transaction history by showing the contents of the Intent, Cart, and Payment mandates. The agent uses the payment_id to retrieve and display what was requested, what was added to the cart, and what was ultimately charged.

Step 3 of 5. Return this step when the agent explains how the authenticity and integrity of the transaction records can be verified — covering how data is signed and how those signatures confirm the records have not been altered. The agent shows that all signatures are valid.
Step 4 of 5. Return this step when the agent actively demonstrates that the ledger cannot be modified or deleted by attempting both operations and showing that both were rejected by the system.

Step 5 of 5. This is the final declared step. Return this step when the agent delivers a closing message after the user confirms their doubts are resolved. The agent does not need to mention MongoDB — this step is triggered by the agent wrapping up the conversation. Once this step appears in the conversation history, the workflow is complete. Any later message must return `in-between-step` with a short closing reply.
